chunks: Surely fulfilment of pledge is the twin of truth,
and I do not know a better shield (against the assaults of sin) than it,
One who realises the reality of return (to the next world) never betrays.
We are in a period when most of the people regard betrayal as wisdom.
In these days the ignorant call it excellence of cunning.
What is the matter with them? Allāh may destroy them.
One who has been through thick and thin of life finds the excuses to be preventing him from orders and prohibitions of Allāh
but he disregards them despite capability (to succumb to them and follows the commands of Allāh),
while one who has no restraints of religion seizes the opportunity (and accepts the excuses for not following the commands of Allāh).

key_terms.الْحُوَّلُ الْقُلَّبُ: one who has experienced many changes/turns of life

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between fulfilling pledges and truth in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines fidelity as the twin of truth and a protective shield, asserting that awareness of the ultimate return prevents treachery. He critiques the societal shift where the ignorant mistakenly equated deceit with cunning, highlighting that true believers restrain themselves from betrayal not due to inability, but out of conscious adherence to divine command. This passage underscores the distinction between mere strategic capability and moral integrity rooted in eschatological consciousness.
